identity.name: Mono- and diacetyltartaric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids (DATEM)
synonyms: Diacetyltartaric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides
identity.chemical_class: Glycerol/fatty acid ester emulsifier mixture containing (di)acetyltartaric acid esters

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic ester components reduce interfacial tension and improve stability of fat-water systems and dough structure.

adi.basis: EFSA 2025 opinion reports ADI 600 mg/kg bw/day for E472e (and E472f), derived from tartaric-acid-based group ADI framework from 2020 re-evaluation.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded estimated dietary exposure for E472e across assessed scenarios and population groups was below ADI, with no safety concern under assessed uses/specification changes.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA chemical page for DATEM shows ADI range 0-50 mg/kg bw and evaluation year 2003.

concerns.summary: A large prospective cohort (NutriNet-Sante) reported a positive association between E472e intake and incident type 2 diabetes (HR 1.04 per 100 mg/day); observational design limits causal inference.
A NutriNet-Sante cohort reported higher CVD risk with E471/E472 group exposure and selected emulsifiers; this is indirect rather than E472e-specific proof.
Human risk hypotheses remain influenced by broader emulsifier-microbiome literature, but direct DATEM-specific mechanistic human evidence is limited.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2020 re-evaluation did not identify adverse effects relevant for humans in available toxicological data for E472a-f.
EFSA 2025 opinion found E472e exposure estimates below ADI in assessed scenarios.
No specific IARC monograph classification was found for DATEM/E472e in the checked IARC classification dataset.

adi_exceedance.notes: Highest reported E472e 95th percentile estimates in EFSA 2025 tables (for example 279.7 mg/kg bw/day in toddlers under Annex II+III maximum-level scenario) remained below the ADI of 600 mg/kg bw/day.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evaluations (EFSA and FDA) remain permissive under defined conditions and EFSA reports below-ADI exposure, but newer observational epidemiology introduces non-trivial uncertainty that does not yet establish causality or justify high-tier classification.
key_factors: EFSA 2025 ADI framework with below-ADI exposure estimates
FDA GRAS status with explicit CFR use conditions
JECFA ADI range reported (0-50 mg/kg bw)
No IARC classification entry found for DATEM
2024 cohort association signal for type 2 diabetes
Evidence for harm remains largely observational or indirect
